_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to methotrexate; may be used as monotherapy or in combination with methotrexate or other nonbiologic DMARDs

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 6-month trial, tofacitinib 5 or 10 mg BID or placebo added to background MTX
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis with inadequate response to at least one approved TNF-inhibiting biologic agent
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoints at Month 3: proportion of patients achieving an ACR20 response, HAQ-DI, and DAS28-4(ESR) less than 2.6
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Month 3 (Study V): placebo 24%, tofacitinib 5 mg BID 41%, tofacitinib 10 mg BID 48%

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 6-month monotherapy trial; tofacitinib 5 or 10 mg BID or placebo (placebo advanced to tofacitinib at Month 3)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis who had an inadequate response to a DMARD (nonbiologic or biologic)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoints at Month 3: proportion of patients achieving ACR20, change in HAQ-DI, and rates of DAS28-4(ESR) less than 2.6
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Month 3 (Study I): placebo 26%, tofacitinib 5 mg BID 59%, tofacitinib 10 mg BID 65%

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 12-month trial; tofacitinib 5 or 10 mg BID or placebo added to background DMARD treatment
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis who had an inadequate response to a nonbiologic DMARD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoints: proportion achieving ACR20 at Month 6, changes in HAQ-DI at Month 3, and rates of DAS28-4(ESR) less than 2.6 at Month 6
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Month 6 (Study II): placebo 31%, tofacitinib 5 mg BID 52%, tofacitinib 10 mg BID 57%

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-comparator 12-month trial; tofacitinib 5 or 10 mg BID, adalimumab 40 mg subcutaneously every other week, or placebo added to background MTX
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis who had an inadequate response to MTX
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoints: proportion achieving ACR20 at Month 6, HAQ-DI at Month 3, and DAS28-4(ESR) less than 2.6 at Month 6
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Month 6 (Study III): placebo 28%, tofacitinib 5 mg BID 50%, tofacitinib 10 mg BID 51%, adalimumab 40 mg 46%

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 2-year trial (planned analysis at 1 year); tofacitinib 5 or 10 mg BID or placebo added to background MTX
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis who had an inadequate response to MTX
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoints: proportion achieving ACR20 at Month 6, mean change from baseline in mTSS at Month 6, HAQ-DI at Month 3, and DAS28-4(ESR) less than 2.6 at Month 6
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Month 6 (Study IV): placebo 24%, tofacitinib 5 mg BID 50%, tofacitinib 10 mg BID 60%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (0-3 months, ≥2%) were upper respiratory tract infections, headache, diarrhea and nasopharyngitis. Most serious adverse reactions were serious infections. Dose-related elevations in lipid parameters and serum creatinine, and decreases in lymphocyte/neutrophil counts were observed.
target_moa: Tofacitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor; JAKs are intracellular enzymes that transmit cytokine/growth factor receptor signals, phosphorylating and activating STATs. Tofacitinib inhibits JAK1 and JAK3 and, to a lesser extent, JAK2 and TyK2.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS INFECTIONS AND MALIGNANCY — serious infections leading to hospitalization or death (including tuberculosis and bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, and other opportunistic infections) have occurred; lymphoma and other malignancies have been observed.

rems.type: A REMS was required to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of serious infections, tuberculosis, malignancy, increase in cholesterol, and decrease in blood counts; the REMS consists of a Medication Guide, communication plan, and timetable for assessments.

advisory_committee.vote: Arthritis Advisory Committee (May 9, 2012): overall efficacy and safety data provided substantial evidence to support approval (8 yes, 2 no); efficacy substantial (10 yes, 0 no); safety substantial (7 yes, 2 no, 1 abstention); radiographic outcome data not substantial (2 yes, 8 no).

summary.text: Tofacitinib, an oral small molecule JAK inhibitor, was approved via a standard full (traditional) approval for moderately to severely active RA after inadequate response or intolerance to methotrexate, based on five Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials demonstrating substantial evidence of efficacy on ACR20 and HAQ-DI; approval included a boxed warning, a REMS, and required postmarketing studies.

citations.quote: Tofacitinib is an oral, small molecule inhibitor of the intracellular tyrosine kinase called Janus kinase (JAK).

This NDA is comprised of 5 Phase 3, randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled trials, designed to assess clinical efficacy and safety of tofacitinib in the target population of adult patients with moderately-to-severely active established RA.

The review of the efficacy data concluded that there is substantial evidence of efficacy of tofacitinib 5 mg or 10 mg for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis based on consistent findings in the domains of reducing signs and symptoms of RA as measured by ACR20, and improving physical function as measured by HAQ-DI.(b) (4)

In accordance with section 505-1 of FDA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Xeljanz (tofacitinib) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of serious infections, including opportunistic infections, tuberculosis, malignancy, increase in cholesterol, and decrease in blood counts.
